title: The fiery furnace (Daniel 3)
hookLine: three young men won't bow, and a fourth walks in the fire with them

lines: A GOLDEN STATUE ON A PLAIN.
cards: A golden statue stands on a plain outside Babylon, sixty cubits high, ninety feet or so. King Nebuchadnezzar has gathered every official in his empire: governors, judges, treasurers. A herald shouts the rule.
When the music starts, horns, pipes, harps, every kind of instrument, everyone falls down and worships the statue. Anyone who doesn't goes into a burning furnace. The music starts.
Thousands drop to the ground at once. And three young men, Jewish exiles who've risen to high posts in Babylon, stay standing. In Babylon they're called Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

teach.b: The furious king gives them one more chance.

Their answer, in the King James Bible: "our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods."
Hear the hinge: but if not. They believe God can save them. They don't claim to know he will.
Their choice doesn't hang on the outcome.
Enraged, the king has the furnace heated seven times hotter, so hot the soldiers who throw them in die in the flames.
Then Nebuchadnezzar leaps up: "Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God." Four. Loose.
Walking. They come out with not a hair singed, their clothes untouched, and, the text says, the smell of fire had not passed on them. Who is the fourth?
The king himself says God sent his angel. In the original Aramaic he says the fourth looks like a son of the gods, how a Babylonian king might describe a heavenly being.
Many Christians, from early on, have seen Christ there, the Son of God present before his birth; others see an angel, as the king says.
Either way, they weren't kept out of the fire.
Someone walked in it with them. Catholic and Orthodox Bibles also include the long song the three men sing in the flames.

how: The story of the three young men is a favorite in Sunday schools, and in Catholic, Orthodox and Anglican worship their song from the furnace, the Benedicite, is sung or said as a canticle; Orthodox Christians sing it in the Christmas season and at the Easter Vigil.

o: the name of the golden statue
a son of the gods, a heavenly being

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: we will not serve thy gods
like a son of the gods

s: the three men say they're sure God will rescue them
they say God is able, but if not, they still won't bow.
they came out without even the smell of fire on them
not a hair singed, their clothes untouched, no smell of fire.
the story says God kept them out of the furnace
they were thrown in. a fourth figure walked with them in the flames.

games.q: the music starts. thousands bow to the king's golden statue. the penalty for standing is the furnace. what do you do?
o: bow on the outside, but not in your heart.
stay standing: God is able, but if not, still no.
games.why: they stay standing, saying God is able to deliver, "but if not... we will not serve thy gods." the choice didn't depend on the outcome.

practice: Think of one small pressure to go along, a joke at someone's expense or a shortcut that isn't honest, and picture yourself standing, quietly, without drama. Notice the fear that comes with it, then picture not being alone in it.
If you pray, ask for courage, and for company in the fire.

wordCard.voice: Bar elahin. Aramaic for a son of the gods: how the king described the fourth figure walking in the flames.

orig.note: Aramaic: a son of the gods, how the king describes the fourth figure. this part of Daniel is in Aramaic.

carryVoice: Your line: a fourth in the fire. Being in the fire doesn't mean being alone in it. See you tomorrow.
